fields.title: Knowledge as code: a structured, validated wiki that AI sessions can read and contribute to

sections.Context: Our engineering knowledge sits in the wiki, in Azure DevOps (ADO) and in people's memory, and nothing connects them. Metadata written in prose cannot be validated or indexed, so hand-kept indexes drift and conventions go unenforced. An AI coding session that cannot find our standards breaks them with confidence. A session that discovers something has nowhere to put it, so the discovery is lost when the session ends.
sections.Decision:
We treat knowledge as code:

* **Every document has a type and validated frontmatter.** The type comes from a
  [taxonomy](https://github.com/paul80nd/knowledge-as-code/blob/c2ced56e10d10784b810828b7b29098b0723712d/examples/engineering/knowledge-as-code/taxonomy.md), and the frontmatter follows a
  [schema](https://github.com/paul80nd/knowledge-as-code/blob/c2ced56e10d10784b810828b7b29098b0723712d/examples/engineering/knowledge-as-code/metadata.md). The type's tier sets its review bar and its lifecycle.
* **Cheap capture happens in the tracker.** A session files an observation as a work item. It becomes a record only
  when a person verifies it.
* **CI validates** the frontmatter, the ids and the links, and generates every index.

[Knowledge as Code](https://github.com/paul80nd/knowledge-as-code/blob/c2ced56e10d10784b810828b7b29098b0723712d/examples/engineering/knowledge-as-code.md) describes the full approach.
sections.Consequences:
* **Every document will acquire a schema obligation.** A contributor picks a type and completes the frontmatter, which
  adds friction in exchange for validation.
* **CI will gate documentation.** A malformed document fails the build, and the first few failures could irritate.
* **Existing ADRs and standards will have to migrate** into records with frontmatter.
* **The value depends on that verification.** If unverified observations reach the corpus, trust in everything else
  falls with them.
* **Session logs will stay out of this corpus**, because they contain credentials and customer data.
